notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.4.0

• Plan selected tickets: check tickets on the Board — one or many, even ones your filters hide — and choose Plan selected. Vekrun works out the order from your tracker's links, flags cycles and likely duplicates, and shows linked tickets you didn't pick (added only if you click). Each repository's tickets become one project plan, and every Work Item shows which tickets it delivers. Nothing is written back to Jira or Asana, and a ticket that changes after you plan blocks the start until you re-analyse.
• xAI (Grok) models: connect your xAI key under Agents → Cloud models. Vekrun uses xAI's Responses API, so a model's reasoning carries across tool calls; xAI's own cost goes into the ledger.
• Grok Build: xAI's coding agent appears under Coding agents for read-only work — investigation, plan critique and review — with every tool request refused.
• Change risk: every Work Item shows how risky its change is, how far it reaches and how sure Vekrun is, kept apart, with the reason for each. A removed permission check is High however small; a formatting-only change stays Low; missing evidence is Unknown, never Low.
• Adaptive verification: the proof now also runs the existing tests that matter for the change's risk, in the same fresh VM, and names the gaps where no test covers a sensitive change.
• Proof manifest: export what a proof rests on — the exact commits, every command with its log hash, the models and providers used, approvals for this exact commit, and what isn't established (vekrun factory proof --format manifest).
• Work Anywhere (preview): under Factory → Workers, check a Linux server read-only — what it can run, which isolation it can use and why, what's exposed — and plan a worker on DigitalOcean or Hetzner using their live prices, with a firewall in place from the first second. Servers are created only within the monthly cap you set.

Fixed
• Factory runs finish on more models: a model that keeps investigating hands over its result on its last turn.
• An acceptance check that breaks itself (a path that doesn't exist, a command that isn't installed) no longer sends correct code back for repair.
